subject: PoC next steps: deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) - ACME Corp
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@acmecorp.com>
Date: 2026-03-02T10:14:00-07:00
Subject: PoC next steps: deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) - ACME Corp

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for the demo today — really helpful to understand ACME's inference workload and constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can lock down a PoC that validates the right deployment mode: hosted API, dedicated capacity, or Private VPC/on-prem.

Recap from our call:
- Primary concern: data residency & strict audit requirements for PII in user transcripts.
- Traffic profile: spiky peak loads (500 TPS peaks during business hours) with steady baseline 40–60 TPS.
- Latency target: 95th percentile < 200ms for short inference (<=512 tokens).
- Cost sensitivity: want to understand unit cost delta between hosted vs dedicated.
- Stakeholders: Alex (ML infra), Priya (Security/compliance), and Prod Eng team (TBD).

Suggested PoC plan (high-level):
1) Goal: prove we can meet latency & throughput SLOs and demonstrate audit/logging requirements.
2) Two-track evaluation: a short hosted API trial (2 weeks) to validate model behavior and REST/SDK integration + a Dedicated capacity or Private VPC PoC (3–4 weeks) to validate throughput, isolation, and security controls.
3) Success criteria (examples):
   - 95p latency <200ms at target load for X model variant
   - End-to-end request tracing + audit logs delivered to your syslog/S3
   - Quantified cost per 1k tokens for typical prompt distribution
   - KV/prefix cache hit rates and improvement in tail latency
4) Timeline: kickoff next week, hosted test immediately; if security gating requires, we can fast-track a Private VPC sandbox environment for smoke tests.

Actions / asks:
- Can you confirm which deployment modes ACME wants to prioritize (Hosted first vs skip to Dedicated/Private)?
- Please share the compliance contact (name + email) who should be on the SOC2/audit calls.
- Any preferred dates for a 30–60 minute PoC kickoff?

I can loop in Marissa (SE) to put together a detailed PoC runbook and attach a draft PoC plan you can review.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Subject: Re: PoC next steps: deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private VPC) - ACME Corp

Ben — thanks for the concise recap. A few clarifications from our side:  

1) Deployment priority: data residency + audit wins. Our security/compliance team will likely require Private VPC or on-prem for production, but we are open to running a hosted pilot for functionality tests first. Ideally: hosted quick test (1–2 weeks) followed immediately by a Private VPC sandbox PoC (3–4 weeks). If Private VPC is too heavy to spin up quickly, Dedicated capacity in our cloud account is acceptable as a middle ground.

2) Success criteria: please add regression tests for hallucination/on-topic behavior (we'll provide ~50 golden prompts), and a stability check under burst load (500 TPS for 5–10 minutes). Also we need token-level cost estimates for each deployment mode.

3) Compliance contact: Priya Singh (cc'd) will own the SOC2 + vendor security questionnaire. Priya, can you share the inventory of required artifacts?

4) Kickoff: available next Tuesday (2026-03-09) or Thursday (2026-03-11) after 11am PT.

Looking forward — please have Marissa draft the PoC plan and include expected infra/networking requirements for Private VPC (VPC peering, subnet sizes, KMS, etc.).

Cheers,
Alex
Alex Johnson
Senior ML Infrastructure Engineer | ACME Corp

Hi Alex / Ben / Priya,

Thanks — looping in a proposed PoC runbook attached (2026-03-03-ACME-Redwood-PoC-Plan.xlsx) and the security overview PDF. High-level notes:

PoC goals (concrete):
- Latency & throughput verification: validate 95p < 200ms at 60 TPS sustained and 500 TPS bursts for short prompts (<=512 tokens).
- Integration & telemetry: end-to-end request tracing, logs forwarded to your S3 bucket and sample events in Splunk/Datadog.
- Security: KMS-managed keys for encryption at rest, VPC peering + private subnets for Private VPC, and support for customer-managed HSM if required.
- Quality: run the 50 golden prompts Alex will provide and show per-prompt pass/fail/regressions.

Proposed schedule:
- Week 0 (kickoff): alignment call, environment access, SOC2 questionnaire exchange.
- Week 1: hosted API quick validation (smoke tests, golden prompts, integration).
- Week 2–4: Private VPC sandbox (or Dedicated if you prefer) — performance/stability tests, telemetry, cost run-rate analysis.

Resource ask from ACME:
- A security contact for questionnaire (Priya) + VPN/VPC network contacts for Private VPC setup.
- Baseline test dataset (golden prompts) and expected load patterns (peak windows).
- Temporary IAM role or short-lived credentials for Redwood to push telemetry to your observability endpoint.

Success criteria (we will capture pass/fail as discrete flags in the runbook):
- Functional: all endpoints respond with expected structured output for >95% of golden prompts.
- Performance: 95p latency < 200ms for target model under defined loads.
- Security: audit logs accessible and encryption keys verified.
- Cost: unit cost estimate within 20% of Redwood's projection for Dedicated/Private vs Hosted.

Attachments: PoC runbook (spreadsheet) + Redwood security overview. I included estimated infra lists for Private VPC (subnet CIDRs, required SG rules, peering steps).

Next steps: Ben / Alex — confirm kickoff slot (you suggested 3/9 or 3/11). Once we confirm, I'll schedule internal SE/infra time and send a calendar invite with the runbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
